Cloud resource provisioning and load balancing both face volatile demand, where dispatching and scheduling decisions must be made online under uncertainty. This paper studies prediction-aware dispatching policies for cloud systems with server-side SRPT scheduling, focusing on how imperfect forecasts affect response time and regret. We propose a lightweight guardrail mechanism that can wrap around standard dispatchers, and we analyze its performance under heavy traffic using a regret-style framework. Empirical experiments on synthetic and trace-driven workloads show that prediction errors vary by workload class and time horizon, while theoretical bounds demonstrate that the augmented policy remains robust and near-optimal in congested regimes.

Modern systems increasingly need both memory-safety enforcement and network visibility, yet practical deployments must balance overhead, coverage, and usability. This paper studies a unified family of hardware-assisted guards that combine address-range validation with compact flow accounting to support both application memory protection and packet-level telemetry. We analyze the design across hardware, operating system, compiler, and runtime layers, focusing on performance overhead, security guarantees, and reconfigurability. The proposed framework presents a generalized family structure with interchangeable policies for memory checks and traffic counters, enabling low-overhead deployment under varied accuracy goals. We also compare the approach with conventional software-only safety and measurement techniques, and outline directions for future architecture extensions that better support adaptive protection and scalable observation.

Modern monitoring and adversarial measurement systems increasingly rely on efficient sketch-based summaries that can support multiple queries over restricted time windows. In this article, we combine interval-aware telemetry with an analysis of covert signal leakage in power-sensitive desktop environments. We propose a unified framework that allows operators to issue drill-down tasks such as heavy hitter detection, entropy estimation, and burst localization for specific periods of interest, while also characterizing how switching-noise patterns can be leveraged for stealthy information transfer across a building's electrical network. Our study presents accuracy guarantees for the telemetry component, evaluates robustness under realistic load variation, and demonstrates how timing- and frequency-based observations can be correlated to identify anomalous activity without intrusive instrumentation. We further discuss practical mitigations including filtering, scheduling, and traffic shaping, along with their limitations.

This article presents a novel blind and robust forensic method for detecting copy-move manipulation in video sequences by focusing on fast motion frames. The approach combines Singular Value Decomposition with a multiresolution decomposition strategy and applies Quantization Index Modulation to selected temporal regions in order to improve efficiency while preserving visual quality. By avoiding redundant processing of all frames, the method reduces computational cost and maintains robustness against compression, noise, filtering, and frame collusion. Experimental evaluation shows strong transparency and reliable detection performance on challenging video forgery cases.

Abstract
Background
Chinese clinical notes contain rich entity-level information and irregular temporal signals that are both useful for downstream prediction tasks. Existing approaches often model these sources separately, which can limit predictive performance and interpretability. This study investigates a hybrid feature representation that combines attention-based sequence encoding with summary statistics extracted from physiological time series.

Methods
We propose a clinical prediction framework that first applies an attention-based CNN-LSTM-CRF module to identify entities in Chinese clinical text, then merges the extracted semantic indicators with a compact set of time series summary statistics. The statistical features include measures of central tendency, dispersion, and distribution shape. We evaluate the resulting representations on three common clinical prediction tasks using cross-validation and a feature selection procedure to identify the most informative feature subsets.

Results
Experiments on electronic health record data showed that the combined representation consistently outperformed text-only and statistics-only baselines. Dispersion-oriented measures were especially useful for short-term deterioration and length-of-stay prediction, while central tendency features contributed more strongly to mortality and diagnosis tasks. The hybrid model produced stable improvements across validation folds and yielded several compact feature combinations with competitive performance.

Conclusion
Combining attention-based clinical entity recognition with carefully chosen temporal summary statistics can improve prediction quality while retaining interpretability. The results suggest that hybrid representations may offer a practical direction for future work in Chinese clinical information extraction and downstream patient risk modeling.

SummaryIn this paper, a hybrid multiport dc-dc converter is proposed for renewable-energy and microgrid interfaces. The topology combines high step-up gain with continuous input current and zero-voltage switching for the main switches. It can interface three dc sources and deliver regulated output under boost and buck-boost modes. The operating principles are analyzed in detail, including steady-state equations, soft-switching conditions, and ripple reduction characteristics. Simulation and experimental results are presented to validate the converter performance in distributed generation applications.

Datacenter operators need efficient methods to diagnose anomalous network behavior and performance stragglers across large clusters. This article presents Merlin, a causal sketching framework that combines interpretable statistical inference with lightweight traffic measurement to identify root causes from job traces and packet-level summaries. The approach targets large-scale production environments, supports both per-flow and aggregate analysis, and emphasizes low-overhead deployment, unbiased diagnosis, and practical tradeoffs between accuracy and space. Experiments on warehouse-scale traces and distributed analytics workloads illustrate how the framework can help isolate bottlenecks, contention, and misconfigured resources in modern datacenters.

Modern systems increasingly need both memory-safety enforcement and network visibility, yet practical deployments must balance overhead, coverage, and usability. This paper studies a unified family of hardware-assisted guards that combine address-range validation with compact flow accounting to support both application memory protection and packet-level telemetry. We analyze the design across hardware, operating system, compiler, and runtime layers, focusing on performance overhead, security guarantees, and reconfigurability. The proposed framework presents a generalized family structure with interchangeable policies for memory checks and traffic counters, enabling low-overhead deployment under varied accuracy goals. We also compare the approach with conventional software-only safety and measurement techniques, and outline directions for future architecture extensions that better support adaptive protection and scalable observation.

Modern monitoring and adversarial measurement systems increasingly rely on efficient sketch-based summaries that can support multiple queries over restricted time windows. In this article, we combine interval-aware telemetry with an analysis of covert signal leakage in power-sensitive desktop environments. We propose a unified framework that allows operators to issue drill-down tasks such as heavy hitter detection, entropy estimation, and burst localization for specific periods of interest, while also characterizing how switching-noise patterns can be leveraged for stealthy information transfer across a building's electrical network. Our study presents accuracy guarantees for the telemetry component, evaluates robustness under realistic load variation, and demonstrates how timing- and frequency-based observations can be correlated to identify anomalous activity without intrusive instrumentation. We further discuss practical mitigations including filtering, scheduling, and traffic shaping, along with their limitations.

Mobile virtual reality (VR) applications increasingly combine sensor-driven interaction with networked content delivery, creating complex traffic patterns in LTE environments. In this fictional study, we examine how Android VR apps disclose motion, scene, and telemetry data over cellular links and ask whether their network requests can reveal the underlying data collection and rendering purposes. We propose NetVR-Purpose, a client-side analysis pipeline that uses URL naming cues, payload structure, and device-side context to infer why a request is sent, while also assessing the latency impact of signaling and offloading in operational 4G LTE networks. Our evaluation blends controlled app traces with expert labeling to classify traffic into multiple purpose categories and quantify the tradeoff between privacy transparency and interactive VR performance. We discuss implications for edge-assisted mobile VR and future 5G deployments.

The device exhibits both reweighting and rewiring effects under electrical stimulation, enabling path following, obstacle avoidance, and rapid response to changing stimulus patterns. By integrating structural plasticity with low-latency memristive dynamics, the proposed system offers a scalable route toward self-adaptive robots and unconventional computing architectures capable of learning from multiple environmental cues.

We study a locally differentially private frequency estimation problem in which a server must recover the most frequent items from a large domain while preserving user privacy. We propose a new randomized sketching algorithm that achieves near-optimal error as a function of the domain size, the privacy budget, and the failure probability. Our approach combines compressed representations of user reports with a refined decoding procedure that improves upon standard count-sketch style baselines. We also establish lower bounds showing that the dependence on the failure probability is unavoidable in the local model. In addition, we derive a transformation that converts a broad class of interactive local protocols into simpler non-interactive mechanisms with only a modest loss in accuracy. These results have applications to histogram release, frequency moments, and robust data analytics under privacy constraints.

Abstract
               Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data analysis often requires both robust imputation of dropout events and accurate cell-type classification. Existing workflows typically address these tasks separately, yet downstream annotation quality can depend strongly on how missing values are handled. In this study, we benchmark a set of imputation-aware single-cell classifiers on diverse scRNA-seq data sets, comparing cluster-level and reference-based strategies under varying dropout rates, class imbalance, and small training cohorts. Results indicate that hybrid methods combining matrix-decomposition imputation with ensemble classification can improve prediction stability, while correlation-based approaches remain competitive when reference labels are noisy. However, no single method consistently detects novel cell populations under all conditions, highlighting the need for adaptive unassigned-label strategies and better integration of denoising with annotation. This work offers practical guidance for selecting methods in scRNA-seq pipelines and suggests future directions for jointly modeling sparsity and cell identity.

AbstractOutdoor visible light sensor networks combine communication, sensing, and environmental exposure in scenarios such as street lighting, vehicle links, and smart-city monitoring. Compared with indoor deployments, these systems face higher interference, variable illumination, weather-driven attenuation, and stronger security risks due to open-channel operation. This article proposes a hybrid authentication and key agreement framework tailored to outdoor VLC-enabled sensor networks. The scheme integrates lightweight mutual authentication, replay resistance, device compromise mitigation, and traceability protection while preserving low communication and computational overhead. Formal verification is provided using ProVerif, and performance is assessed against related protocols in terms of message complexity, storage cost, and security properties. The study also discusses deployment considerations for fog, rain, haze, and solar-powered receivers, and identifies research opportunities for resilient Li-Fi based sensing infrastructures.

Each agent chooses an arm, decides whether to communicate, and updates its policy using only its own history together with limited peer observations. We propose a collaborative exploration protocol that shares compact arm summaries rather than raw rewards, enabling reduced regret under constrained bandwidth. The analysis characterizes per-agent regret as a function of the number of agents, the number of arms, the horizon, and the communication sparsity, and compares the method against both fully independent learning and fully connected information sharing. Empirical results on synthetic networked bandit instances show that minimal collaboration can substantially improve sample efficiency without incurring the cost of global synchronization.

Cloud resource provisioning and load balancing both face volatile demand, where dispatching and scheduling decisions must be made online under uncertainty. This paper studies prediction-aware dispatching policies for cloud systems with server-side SRPT scheduling, focusing on how imperfect forecasts affect response time and regret. We propose a lightweight guardrail mechanism that can wrap around standard dispatchers, and we analyze its performance under heavy traffic using a regret-style framework. Empirical experiments on synthetic and trace-driven workloads show that prediction errors vary by workload class and time horizon, while theoretical bounds demonstrate that the augmented policy remains robust and near-optimal in congested regimes.

This article surveys device concepts, circuit integration, and system-level organization for hybrid in-memory computing and soft robotic elements. Emphasis is placed on synaptic behavior, feedback-enabled actuation, and scalable architectures suitable for biomimetic sensing, learning, and movement in distributed edge systems.
